records.source: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ἐν Καισαρείᾳ ὀνόματι Κορνήλιος, ἑκατοντάρχης ἐκ σπείρης τῆς καλουμένης Ἰταλικῆς, εὐσεβὴς καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν σὺν παντὶ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνας πολλὰς τῷ λαῷ καὶ δεόμενος τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ παντός, εἶδεν ἐν ὁράματι φανερῶς ὡσεὶ περὶ ὥραν ἐνάτην τῆς ἡμέρας ἄγγελον τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθόντα πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ εἰπόντα αὐτῷ· Κορνήλιε.
records.gloss: A man now certain in Caesarea by name Cornelius, a centurion of [the] cohort the being called Italian, \v 2 devout and fearing the God with all the household of him, doing alms many to the people and praying to the God through all, \v 3 saw in a vision clearly about [the] hour ninth of the day an angel of the God having come in to him and having said to him, Cornelius.
pieces: In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Cohort.
He was a devout man who feared God, as did his whole household. He gave generously to the poor among the Jewish people and prayed to God at all times.
One afternoon at about three o'clock he had a vision. He saw plainly an angel of God come in to him and say, "Cornelius!"

L.1: Now a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian [cohort],
L.2: devout and fearing God with all his household, doing many [acts of] alms for the people and praying to God continually,
L.3: saw clearly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in to him and saying to him, "Cornelius."

R.1: There was a man named Cornelius who lived in the city of Caesarea. He was a centurion, an officer over about a hundred Roman soldiers. His unit was called the Italian Cohort.
R.2: Cornelius was not a Jew, but he and everyone in his house worshiped the God of Israel. He often gave money to help poor Jewish people, and he prayed to God all the time.
R.3: One day at about three o'clock in the afternoon, Cornelius saw a vision. He clearly saw an angel from God come into his house. The angel said to him, "Cornelius!"

decisions.choice: a centurion of the Italian cohort: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers, in a unit raised from Roman citizens in Italy
decisions.reason: A cohort was a unit of about six hundred soldiers, and a centurion commanded about a hundred. An inscription names a second Italian cohort of Roman citizens stationed in Syria in the first century. Caesarea was the seat of the Roman governor of Judea.

decisions.choice: fearing God: a Gentile who worshiped the God of Israel without becoming a Jew
decisions.reason: Luke uses this phrase and its like for Gentiles who joined in Jewish worship and prayer (13:16, 13:26, 16:14, 17:4, 18:7). Cornelius was not circumcised: 10:28 and 11:3 treat him as a Gentile. He is one of the God-fearers.

decisions.choice: doing many alms to the people: giving generously to the poor of the Jewish people
alternatives: gifts to the people in general
decisions.reason: "The people" in Luke and Acts usually means the people of Israel (as in 10:41-42). Alms are gifts given out of mercy to the poor (3:2).

decisions.choice: about the ninth hour of the day: about three in the afternoon, the hour of prayer
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise. The ninth hour was the time of the afternoon prayer at the temple (3:1). Cornelius says in 10:30 that he was praying then.

decisions.choice: clearly: plainly, not in a dream
decisions.reason: Cornelius is awake and sees the angel distinctly.

decisions.choice: a devout man who feared God
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the phrase close to the Greek here and lets the meaning note say he was a Gentile; the following verses make it plain.

decisions.choice: an officer over about a hundred Roman soldiers; was not a Jew, but ... worshiped the God of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable explains the rank and says outright that Cornelius was a Gentile who worshiped Israel's God, as 10:28 and 11:3 show.

decisions.choice: about three o'clock in the afternoon
alternatives: about the ninth hour of the day
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the clock time; Literal keeps the Greek count of hours, as at 3:1.

records.heading: An angel comes to Cornelius

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἔμφοβος γενόμενος εἶπεν· Τί ἐστιν, κύριε;
records.gloss: He and having looked intently at him and afraid having become said, What is it, lord?
pieces: Cornelius stared at him in fear and said, "What is it, sir?"

L.4: And he, staring at him and becoming afraid, said, "What is it, lord?"

R.4: Cornelius looked hard at the angel. He was afraid. He said, "What is it, sir?"

decisions.choice: lord: a respectful address to a heavenly visitor, like "sir"
decisions.reason: Cornelius speaks to the angel he sees, not to God. The same word is a polite address to a superior (16:30).

decisions.choice: sir
decisions.reason: Since Cornelius is speaking to the angel, Balanced and Readable use a polite address. Literal keeps the Greek word in lower case.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Αἱ προσευχαί σου καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἀνέβησαν εἰς μνημόσυνον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: He said then to him, The prayers of you and the alms of you have gone up for a memorial before the God.
pieces: The angel answered, "Your prayers and your gifts to the poor have risen before God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has remembered you.

L.4: And he said to him, "Your prayers and your alms have gone up as a memorial before God.

R.4: The angel said, "God has heard your prayers. He has seen the gifts you give to poor people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembers you.

decisions.choice: have gone up as a memorial before God: like an offering whose smoke rises to God
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses this word for the memorial portion of the grain offering, burned so that it rises to God (Leviticus 2:2, 2:9, 2:16). Prayer is pictured as rising incense in Psalm 141:2.

decisions.choice: God has taken notice of Cornelius's prayers and gifts
decisions.reason: The angel says God remembers him; 10:31 repeats it. The point is that God has heard him, and so he sends him to Peter for the message by which he will be saved (11:14).

decisions.choice: and he has remembered you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the offering picture means; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: "Alms" is no longer common English; Literal keeps it.

records.source: καὶ νῦν πέμψον ἄνδρας εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνά τινα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος·
records.gloss: And now send men to Joppa and summon Simon a certain who is called Peter.
pieces: Now send some men to Joppa and have them bring back a man named Simon, the one called Peter.

L.5: And now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon who is called Peter.

R.5: Now send some men to the town of Joppa. Tell them to bring back a man named Simon. People also call him Peter.

decisions.choice: Joppa: a port on the coast, about thirty miles south of Caesarea
decisions.reason: Peter had been staying there since raising Tabitha (9:36-43). The journey took about a day and a half (10:9, 10:23-24, 10:30).

decisions.choice: have them bring back
decisions.reason: The verb means to send for someone; Balanced says who will fetch him.

records.source: οὗτος ξενίζεται παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ, ᾧ ἐστιν οἰκία παρὰ θάλασσαν.
records.gloss: This one lodges with a certain Simon a tanner, whose is [a] house by [the] sea.
pieces: He is a guest of another Simon, a tanner, whose house stands by the sea."

L.6: He is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by [the] sea."

R.6: He is staying with a man who makes leather. That man is also named Simon, and his house is near the sea."

decisions.choice: a tanner: a man who made leather from the hides of animals
decisions.reason: Peter has stayed with him for some time (9:43). Handling dead animals could make a person ritually unclean (Leviticus 11:39-40), so Luke may mention his trade to show that Peter was already living with a man many would avoid; the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT ends the angel's words here
alternatives: some late manuscripts add "he will tell you what you must do"
decisions.reason: A few late manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add these words, perhaps from 9:6 or 11:14. The early manuscripts do not have them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man who makes leather
decisions.reason: Readable explains the trade.

records.source: ὡς δὲ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ λαλῶν αὐτῷ, φωνήσας δύο τῶν οἰκετῶν καὶ στρατιώτην εὐσεβῆ τῶν προσκαρτερούντων αὐτῷ καὶ ἐξηγησάμενος ἅπαντα αὐτοῖς ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Ἰόππην.
records.gloss: When then departed the angel the [one] speaking to him, having called two of the household servants and a soldier devout of those attending on him, \v 8 and having explained all things to them he sent them to Joppa.
pieces: As soon as the angel who had spoken to him was gone, Cornelius called two of his household servants and one of the soldiers who attended him, a devout man.
He told them all that had happened and sent them off to Joppa.

L.7: And when the angel who was speaking to him had gone, he called two of [his] household servants and a devout soldier from among those who waited on him,
L.8: and having explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

R.7: When the angel left, Cornelius called two of his servants. He also called one of his soldiers. This soldier worshiped God too.
R.8: Cornelius told them everything that had happened. Then he sent them to Joppa.

decisions.choice: household servants: members of the household staff, very likely slaves
decisions.reason: The word means someone who serves in a house; in a Roman household such servants were usually slaves. It is not the usual word for slave, so the rendering keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: devout: like Cornelius, one who worshiped God
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same word of Cornelius in 10:2.

decisions.choice: those who waited on him: soldiers in his personal service
alternatives: soldiers who were constantly with him in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay close to someone and attend him.

decisions.choice: worshiped God too
decisions.reason: Readable says what "devout" means here, as in 10:2.

records.source: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ὁδοιπορούντων ἐκείνων καὶ τῇ πόλει ἐγγιζόντων ἀνέβη Πέτρος ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα προσεύξασθαι περὶ ὥραν ἕκτην.
records.gloss: On the now next day, journeying those and to the city drawing near, went up Peter onto the housetop to pray about [the] hour sixth.
pieces: The next day, while the men were still on the road and nearing the town, Peter went up on the roof to pray. It was about noon.

L.9: Now on the next day, while they were on their way and drawing near to the city, Peter went up onto the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour.

R.9: The next day, the men were traveling and were getting close to Joppa. At about twelve o'clock noon, Peter went up on the flat roof of the house to pray.

decisions.choice: the housetop: the flat roof of the house, used as a quiet place
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs reached by outside stairs, where people could work, rest or pray.

decisions.choice: about the sixth hour: about noon
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise. Psalm 55:18 speaks of praying evening, morning and noon; noon was not one of the set temple hours.

decisions.choice: about noon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the clock time; Literal keeps the Greek count of hours.

decisions.choice: Joppa
decisions.reason: Readable names the town.

records.heading: What God has made clean

records.source: ἐγένετο δὲ πρόσπεινος καὶ ἤθελεν γεύσασθαι· παρασκευαζόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐγένετο ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἔκστασις, καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγμένον καὶ καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιέμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἐν ᾧ ὑπῆρχεν πάντα τὰ τετράποδα καὶ ἑρπετὰ τῆς γῆς καὶ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
records.gloss: He became then hungry and was wanting to eat; preparing but they, came upon him a trance, \v 11 and he sees the heaven opened and coming down a vessel certain as a sheet great, by four corners being let down upon the earth, \v 12 in which were all the four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and birds of the heaven.
pieces: He grew hungry and wanted something to eat. While the food was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
He saw heaven standing open and something like a large sheet coming down, lowered to the ground by its four corners.
In it were all kinds of four-footed animals, creatures that crawl on the ground, and birds of the air.

L.10: And he became hungry and wanted to eat; but while they were preparing [the meal], a trance came upon him,
L.11: and he sees heaven opened and a certain object coming down like a great sheet, being let down by four corners onto the earth,
L.12: in which were all the four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and birds of the sky.

R.10: Peter became hungry and wanted to eat. While the food was being made ready, God gave him a vision, and he saw things no one else could see.
R.11: He saw the sky open up. Something that looked like a big sheet was coming down. It was held by its four corners and was being let down to the ground.
R.12: In it were all kinds of animals: animals with four legs, animals that crawl on the ground, and birds.

decisions.choice: a trance: a state in which God showed him a vision
decisions.reason: Peter calls what he saw a vision (10:17, 10:19), and in 11:5 he says, "in a trance I saw a vision". Luke uses the same word in 22:17 for Paul praying in the temple.

decisions.choice: he sees: the present tense in the story, to make the scene vivid
decisions.reason: Greek often tells a past event in the present tense. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past.

decisions.choice: all the four-footed animals, creeping things and birds: every kind of living creature, clean and unclean together
decisions.reason: The list recalls the creatures of Genesis 1:24-30 and 6:20. The law divided such animals into clean and unclean (Leviticus 11). Here they are all mixed together, which is why Peter refuses in 10:14.

decisions.choice: heaven: the sky as the place from which God speaks
decisions.reason: The same word means both sky and heaven. The voice comes from there (11:9), and the sheet is taken back up into it (10:16).

decisions.choice: God gave him a vision, and he saw things no one else could see
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a trance was here, as 11:5 does.

decisions.choice: all kinds of
decisions.reason: The Greek "all" means every kind of creature, not every single animal on earth.

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
records.gloss: And came a voice to him, Having risen up, Peter, kill and eat.
pieces: Then a voice said to him, "Get up, Peter. Slaughter and eat."

L.13: And a voice came to him, "Get up, Peter; kill and eat."

R.13: Then a voice spoke to him. It said, "Get up, Peter. Kill some of these animals and eat them."

decisions.choice: kill: slaughter an animal for food
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to sacrifice, but here, with "eat", it means to slaughter for a meal, as in Luke 15:23.

decisions.choice: a voice: the voice of the Lord, from heaven
decisions.reason: Peter answers "Lord" (10:14), and the voice speaks with God's authority about what God has made clean (10:15).

decisions.choice: kill some of these animals and eat them
decisions.reason: Readable names the objects the Greek leaves understood.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Μηδαμῶς, κύριε, ὅτι οὐδέποτε ἔφαγον πᾶν κοινὸν καὶ ἀκάθαρτον.
records.gloss: The but Peter said, By no means, Lord, for never did I eat anything common and unclean.
pieces: "Certainly not, Lord!" Peter replied. "Nothing unholy or unclean has ever passed my lips."

L.14: But Peter said, "By no means, Lord, for I have never eaten anything common or unclean."

R.14: But Peter said, "No, Lord! I could never do that! I have never eaten anything that our law calls unholy or unclean."

decisions.choice: common or unclean: food the law of Moses forbade, not set apart for God's people
decisions.reason: "Common" means profane, the opposite of holy; "unclean" is the law's word for forbidden animals (Leviticus 11). Together they name what a faithful Jew would not eat.

decisions.choice: the words of Ezekiel, who refused unclean food
decisions.reason: When God told Ezekiel to eat food made unclean, the prophet protested to the Lord God that no unclean meat had ever entered his mouth (Ezekiel 4:14). Peter answers the same way, and the voice answers him differently.

decisions.choice: Lord: the one speaking from heaven, whom Peter recognizes as the Lord
decisions.reason: Peter is answering a voice from heaven, and his refusal is like Ezekiel's to the Lord God. He does not yet understand what the Lord is telling him.

decisions.choice: Certainly not, Lord! ... Nothing unholy or unclean has ever passed my lips.
alternatives: I have never eaten anything common or unclean
decisions.reason: Balanced puts Peter's exclamation first and uses "unholy" for "common" (as in 11:8), which in modern English could mean ordinary.

decisions.choice: anything that our law calls unholy or unclean
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the law of Moses forbade these foods.

records.source: καὶ φωνὴ πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
records.gloss: And a voice again for a second [time] to him, What the God cleansed, you not call common.
pieces: The voice spoke to him a second time: "What God has made clean, you must not call unholy."

L.15: And a voice [came] to him again a second time, "What God has cleansed, do not call common."

R.15: The voice spoke to Peter again. It said, "God has made these things clean. So you must not say that they are unholy."

decisions.choice: do not call common: stop treating as unclean
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" can forbid what someone is already doing. Peter has just called these animals unclean.

decisions.choice: what God has made clean: God has declared these foods clean, and, as Peter learns, the people they stand for
decisions.reason: Peter explains the vision in 10:28: he must not call any person common or unclean. Jesus had already declared all foods clean (Mark 7:19), and 15:9 says God cleansed the hearts of the Gentiles by faith. The vision is about food and also about people.

decisions.choice: made clean
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plainer phrase; Literal keeps "cleansed".

records.source: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνελήμφθη τὸ σκεῦος εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
records.gloss: This now happened three times, and immediately was taken up the vessel into the heaven.
pieces: This happened three times, and then at once the sheet was taken back up into heaven.

L.16: Now this happened three times, and immediately the object was taken up into heaven.

R.16: This happened three times. Then the sheet was quickly taken back up into the sky.

decisions.choice: three times: the whole exchange happened three times
alternatives: only the voice spoke three times
decisions.reason: The threefold repetition makes the lesson certain; compare Genesis 41:32 on a dream given twice.

decisions.choice: heaven: where the sheet came from, the sky as God's dwelling
decisions.reason: As in 10:11. Readable says "sky"; the meaning is the same place.

decisions.choice: the sheet
decisions.reason: The word means a container or object; 10:11 says it was like a sheet, and Balanced and Readable call it that.

records.source: Ὡς δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ διηπόρει ὁ Πέτρος τί ἂν εἴη τὸ ὅραμα ὃ εἶδεν, ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Κορνηλίου διερωτήσαντες τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ Σίμωνος ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὸν πυλῶνα, καὶ φωνήσαντες ἐπυνθάνοντο εἰ Σίμων ὁ ἐπικαλούμενος Πέτρος ἐνθάδε ξενίζεται.
records.gloss: While now in himself was perplexed the Peter what might be the vision which he saw, behold, the men the having been sent by the Cornelius, having asked for the house of the Simon, stood at the gate, \v 18 and having called out they were asking if Simon the [one] being called Peter here is lodging.
pieces: Peter was still wondering what to make of the vision he had seen when the men sent by Cornelius, who had found their way to Simon's house, arrived at the gate.
They called out, asking whether Simon known as Peter was a guest there.

L.17: Now while Peter was puzzling within himself what the vision that he had seen might be, look, the men sent by Cornelius, having asked their way to Simon's house, stood at the gate,
L.18: and calling out, they were asking whether Simon, who is called Peter, was lodging there.

R.17: Peter did not understand what the vision meant. He was still thinking about it when the men from Cornelius arrived. They had asked people where Simon the leather-maker's house was. Now they were standing at the gate.
R.18: They called out, "Is Simon Peter staying here?"

decisions.choice: was perplexed: was at a loss, unable to work it out
decisions.reason: The verb means to be completely puzzled, as in 2:12 and 5:24.

decisions.choice: behold: draws attention to the timing; the men arrive just then
decisions.reason: God's timing joins the two visions: as Peter wonders, the answer is at the door.

decisions.choice: they were asking whether Simon was lodging there: a reported question
decisions.reason: Luke reports the question indirectly. Readable turns it into their own words, which says the same thing.

decisions.choice: "Is Simon Peter staying here?"
alternatives: they were asking whether Simon, who is called Peter, was lodging there
decisions.reason: Readable gives the reported question as direct speech, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: no word for "look"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the timing by the shape of the sentence.

records.source: τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διενθυμουμένου περὶ τοῦ ὁράματος εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὸ πνεῦμα· Ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες ζητοῦντές σε·
records.gloss: The and Peter thinking over about the vision, said to him the Spirit, Behold, men are seeking you;
pieces: While Peter was still turning the vision over in his mind, the Spirit said to him, "Some men are here looking for you.

L.19: And while Peter was thinking over the vision, the Spirit said to him, "Look, men are looking for you;

R.19: Peter was still thinking about the vision. Then the Holy Spirit said to him, "Some men are here looking for you.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "men", with no number
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts read "three men", which agrees with 10:7 (two servants and a soldier) and 11:11; one early manuscript reads "two", perhaps counting only the servants. Other manuscripts, followed by the SBLGNT, have no number. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: the Holy Spirit, who speaks and directs
decisions.reason: The Spirit says "I have sent them" (10:20), and Peter says in 11:12 that the Spirit told him to go. As in 8:29 and 13:2, the Spirit speaks as a person.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable names the Spirit in full.

records.source: ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς κατάβηθι καὶ πορεύου σὺν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς.
records.gloss: but having risen up go down and go with them, nothing doubting, because I have sent them.
pieces: Get up, go downstairs, and go with them without any hesitation, because I have sent them."

L.20: but get up, go down, and go with them, not hesitating at all, for I have sent them."

R.20: Get up and go downstairs. Go with them. Do not be afraid or doubt anything, because I have sent them."

decisions.choice: not hesitating at all: without doubting or holding back
alternatives: without making any distinction between Jew and Gentile
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to doubt or waver (Romans 4:20). In 11:12 Peter repeats the command with an active form of the same verb, which can mean "making no distinction", and 15:9 says God made no distinction between Jew and Gentile. A play on both senses is possible.

decisions.choice: I have sent them: the Spirit himself sent the men
decisions.reason: Cornelius sent them (10:8), but he did so at God's command. The Spirit claims the sending as his own.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid or doubt anything
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what hesitating would mean for Peter.

records.source: καταβὰς δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ εἰμι ὃν ζητεῖτε· τίς ἡ αἰτία δι’ ἣν πάρεστε;
records.gloss: Having gone down then Peter to the men said, Behold, I am [the one] whom you seek; what [is] the reason for which you are here?
pieces: So Peter went down to the men and said, "I am the man you are looking for. Why have you come?"

L.21: Then Peter went down to the men and said, "Look, I am [the one] whom you are seeking; what is the reason for which you are here?"

R.21: So Peter went down to the men. He said, "I am the man you are looking for. Why are you here?"

decisions.choice: what is the reason: why have you come?
decisions.reason: The word can mean a cause or a charge, but here it is a simple question about their errand, as their answer shows.

decisions.choice: Why have you come?
alternatives: What is the reason for which you are here?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the question plainly.

records.source: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης, ἀνὴρ δίκαιος καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν μαρτυρούμενός τε ὑπὸ ὅλου τοῦ ἔθνους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐχρηματίσθη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου ἁγίου μεταπέμψασθαί σε εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ῥήματα παρὰ σοῦ.
records.gloss: They and said, Cornelius a centurion, a man righteous and fearing the God, being well spoken of and by all the nation of the Jews, was divinely instructed by an angel holy to summon you to the house of him and to hear words from you.
pieces: They replied, "We come from Cornelius the centurion, an upright man who fears God and is respected by all the Jewish people. A holy angel instructed him to send for you to come to his house, so that he could hear what you have to say."

L.22: And they said, "Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one who fears God, well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews, was directed by a holy angel to summon you to his house and to hear words from you."

R.22: They answered, "We were sent by Cornelius. He is a Roman officer. He is a good man who worships God, and all the Jewish people respect him. A holy angel told him to ask you to come to his house. He wants to hear what you have to say."

decisions.choice: a righteous man: an upright man who does what is right before God
alternatives: one who keeps the whole law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word describes his character and conduct. Luke uses it of Zechariah and Elizabeth (Luke 1:6) and of Simeon (Luke 2:25).

decisions.choice: was directed: was told by God, through the angel
decisions.reason: The verb is used of instruction that comes from God (Matthew 2:12, Luke 2:26, Hebrews 8:5).

decisions.choice: to hear words from you: to hear the message Peter has to give
decisions.reason: In 11:14 Peter reports that the angel spoke of words by which Cornelius and his household would be saved.

decisions.choice: an upright man
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plain word for a person's conduct; the Greek word here is not the key term "righteousness".

decisions.choice: We were sent by Cornelius
decisions.reason: Readable adds who sent them, which the Greek leaves understood, and explains "centurion" as "Roman officer".

records.source: εἰσκαλεσάμενος οὖν αὐτοὺς ἐξένισεν.
records.gloss: Having called in therefore them he lodged [them].
pieces: Peter invited them in and had them stay as his guests.

L.23: So having invited them in, he gave [them] lodging.

R.23: Peter asked them to come into the house, and they stayed there that night as his guests.

decisions.choice: he gave them lodging: Peter, a Jew, took Gentile visitors in as guests
decisions.reason: Two of the men were household servants of a Gentile, and the soldier was a Gentile too. Taking them in as guests, and probably eating with them, was already a step toward what Peter says in 10:28.

decisions.choice: that night
decisions.reason: 10:23 goes on to the next day, so they stayed the night.

records.source: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς, καί τινες τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἀπὸ Ἰόππης συνῆλθον αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: On the now next day having risen up he went out with them, and some of the brothers of those from Joppa went with him.
pieces: The next day he set out with them, and some of the believers from Joppa came along with him.

L.23: And on the next day he got up and went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went with him.

R.23: The next day Peter left with the three men. Some of the believers from Joppa went along with him.

decisions.choice: the brothers: fellow believers from the church in Joppa
decisions.reason: In 11:12 Peter says six brothers went with him; they are witnesses to what happened (10:45).

decisions.choice: believers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who these were; they may all have been men (11:12), so no gender setting is used.

decisions.choice: the three men
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" refers to: two household servants and a soldier (10:7).

records.heading: Peter goes to a Gentile's house

records.source: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν.
records.gloss: On the now next day he entered into the Caesarea.
pieces: The day after that, he arrived in Caesarea.

L.24: And on the next day he entered Caesarea.

R.24: On the day after that, Peter arrived in Caesarea.

decisions.choice: the next day: the journey of about thirty miles took Peter and the men part of two days
decisions.reason: They left Joppa on one day and arrived the next. 10:30 counts four days from the vision to Peter's arrival, counting both the first and last days.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Κορνήλιος ἦν προσδοκῶν αὐτοὺς συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς συγγενεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἀναγκαίους φίλους.
records.gloss: The but Cornelius was expecting them, having called together the relatives of him and the close friends.
pieces: Cornelius was waiting for them and had gathered his relatives and close friends.

L.24: And Cornelius was expecting them, having called together his relatives and close friends.

R.24: Cornelius was waiting for them. He had invited his relatives and close friends to come to his house.

decisions.choice: close friends: intimate friends
decisions.reason: The word literally means "necessary", but with "friends" it means close ones.

decisions.choice: was expecting them: he was confident they would come
decisions.reason: He had already gathered people to hear Peter.

records.source: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο τοῦ εἰσελθεῖν τὸν Πέτρον, συναντήσας αὐτῷ ὁ Κορνήλιος πεσὼν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας προσεκύνησεν.
records.gloss: As then it happened the entering the Peter, having met him the Cornelius, having fallen at the feet, worshiped.
pieces: As Peter came in, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and bowed down before him.

L.25: And as Peter was entering, Cornelius met him and, falling at [his] feet, worshiped [him].

R.25: When Peter was about to go into the house, Cornelius came to meet him. He knelt down at Peter's feet and bowed low to the ground to show him honor.

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down to the ground in reverence
alternatives: offered him worship as to a god
decisions.reason: The verb can mean full worship or the deep bow given to a great person. Cornelius may have taken Peter for a messenger from heaven, so Peter's reply in 10:26 refuses more than ordinary respect.

decisions.choice: bowed down before him / bowed low to show him honor
decisions.reason: "Worship" in English means only what is given to God; Balanced and Readable describe the act, and the meaning note gives the other reading.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι· καὶ ἐγὼ αὐτὸς ἄνθρωπός εἰμι.
records.gloss: The but Peter raised up him saying, Stand up; also I myself a man am.
pieces: But Peter pulled him to his feet. "Stand up," he said. "I am only a human being myself."

L.26: But Peter raised him up, saying, "Stand up; I myself am also a man."

R.26: But Peter helped him get up. He said, "Stand up. I am just a man, like you."

decisions.choice: I am also a man: I am only human, not one to be worshiped
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas say the same at Lystra (14:15), and an angel refuses worship in Revelation 19:10. Only God is to be worshiped.

decisions.choice: a human being
decisions.reason: Peter's point is that he is human, not that he is male; Balanced makes that plain. Literal and Readable keep "man", which Peter is.

records.source: καὶ συνομιλῶν αὐτῷ εἰσῆλθεν, καὶ εὑρίσκει συνεληλυθότας πολλούς, ἔφη τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὡς ἀθέμιτόν ἐστιν ἀνδρὶ Ἰουδαίῳ κολλᾶσθαι ἢ προσέρχεσθαι ἀλλοφύλῳ· κἀμοὶ ὁ θεὸς ἔδειξεν μηδένα κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον λέγειν ἄνθρωπον·
records.gloss: And talking with him he went in and finds having come together many, \v 28 he was saying and to them, You know how unlawful it is for a man Jew to associate with or to come to a foreigner; and to me the God showed no one common or unclean to call person;
pieces: Still talking with him, Peter went inside and found a large gathering of people.
He said to them, "You know well that it is not permitted for a Jew to keep company with a foreigner or to enter a foreigner's home. But God has shown me that I must not call anyone unholy or unclean.

L.27: And talking with him, he went in and finds many [people] gathered,
L.28: and he said to them, "You yourselves know how forbidden it is for a Jewish man to associate with or visit a foreigner; but God has shown me that I should call no {{gender:person|man}} common or unclean.

R.27: Peter kept talking with Cornelius as they went inside. There Peter found many people who had come together.
R.28: He said to them, "You know that our Jewish ways do not allow a Jew to visit people from other nations or to spend time with them. But God has shown me that I must not say that any person is not clean.

decisions.choice: forbidden for a Jew to associate with or visit a foreigner: a strict custom that kept Jews apart from Gentiles, especially at meals and in their homes
alternatives: a command written in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The law of Moses does not forbid all contact with Gentiles, but many Jews avoided entering Gentile homes or eating with Gentiles because of food laws and the risk of impurity (11:3; John 18:28; Galatians 2:12). The word means contrary to accepted custom or religious practice.

decisions.choice: God has shown me: Peter now understands the vision; it was about people, not only food
decisions.reason: Peter uses the words of the vision, "common or unclean" (10:14-15), of people. God, not Peter, has drawn the line where it now lies.

decisions.choice: a Jewish man: any Jew
decisions.reason: The custom applied to Jews in general; the word "man" here means a person of that nation.

decisions.choice: a Jew
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the meaning note; Literal keeps "man".

decisions.choice: anyone / any person
decisions.reason: The Greek word means a human being; Balanced and Readable use an inclusive word, and Literal has the gender setting.

decisions.choice: our Jewish ways do not allow
alternatives: our Jewish law does not allow
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that this was a rule of Jewish life. It avoids "law", since the meaning note says it was custom more than a written command.

records.source: διὸ καὶ ἀναντιρρήτως ἦλθον μεταπεμφθείς πυνθάνομαι οὖν τίνι λόγῳ μετεπέμψασθέ με.
records.gloss: Therefore also without objecting I came having been summoned. I ask therefore for what reason you summoned me?
pieces: That is why I came without raising any objection when you sent for me. So may I ask why you sent for me?"

L.29: Therefore I also came without objection when I was sent for. So I ask, for what reason did you send for me?"

R.29: That is why I came when you asked me to come, and I did not argue about it. Now please tell me: why did you ask me to come?"

decisions.choice: therefore: because of what God showed him, Peter came
decisions.reason: The vision and the Spirit's word (10:20) removed his objection.

decisions.choice: without objection: without speaking against it
decisions.reason: The word means without contradicting.

records.source: Καὶ ὁ Κορνήλιος ἔφη· Ἀπὸ τετάρτης ἡμέρας μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ὥρας ἤμην τὴν ἐνάτην προσευχόμενος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἔστη ἐνώπιόν μου ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ καὶ φησί· Κορνήλιε, εἰσηκούσθη σου ἡ προσευχὴ καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἐμνήσθησαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: And the Cornelius was saying, From fourth day until this the hour I was the ninth praying in the house of me, and behold, a man stood before me in clothing bright \v 31 and says, Cornelius, has been heard your the prayer and the alms of you have been remembered before the God.
pieces: Cornelius answered, "Four days ago, at this very hour, three in the afternoon, I was in my house praying. Suddenly a man in shining clothes stood in front of me.
He said, 'Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and has remembered your gifts to the poor.

L.30: And Cornelius said, "Four days ago, until this hour, I was praying the ninth [hour prayer] in my house, and look, a man stood before me in bright clothing
L.31: and says, 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your alms have been remembered before God.

R.30: Cornelius said, "Four days ago, at this same time, three o'clock in the afternoon, I was praying in my house. All at once a man in bright, shining clothes was standing in front of me.
R.31: He said, 'Cornelius, God has heard your prayer. He has seen the gifts you give to poor people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembers them.

decisions.choice: from the fourth day until this hour: four days ago, at this same time of day
alternatives: he prayed without stopping for four days
decisions.reason: The phrase counts back to the same hour four days before, counting both the first and the last day (10:3, 10:9, 10:23-24). The Greek is compressed, and "the ninth" names the hour of prayer, as in 10:3.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "praying"
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "fasting and praying"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "I was fasting, and at the ninth hour I was praying". The early manuscripts do not have "fasting". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man in bright clothing: the angel of 10:3, appearing as a man
decisions.reason: Angels appear as men in shining clothes in Luke 24:4 and Acts 1:10. Luke has already called him an angel (10:3).

decisions.choice: has been heard ... remembered before God: God has heard and taken notice
alternatives: God has rewarded his good works
decisions.reason: The passive verbs mean that God has done this, as 10:4 says.

decisions.choice: God has heard ... has remembered
alternatives: has been heard ... have been remembered before God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who acts, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps the passives.

decisions.choice: three in the afternoon
decisions.reason: As at 10:3.

records.source: πέμψον οὖν εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετακάλεσαι Σίμωνα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος· οὗτος ξενίζεται ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος βυρσέως παρὰ θάλασσαν.
records.gloss: Send therefore to Joppa and call for Simon who is called Peter; this one lodges in [the] house of Simon a tanner by [the] sea.
pieces: So send to Joppa and ask Simon, who is called Peter, to come. He is staying as a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.'

L.32: So send to Joppa and call for Simon, who is called Peter; he is lodging in the house of Simon, a tanner, by [the] sea.'

R.32: Send some men to Joppa to bring back Simon, who is also called Peter. He is staying in the house of a man named Simon, who makes leather. His house is near the sea.'

decisions.choice: SBLGNT ends the angel's words here
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "he will speak to you when he comes"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "who, when he comes, will speak to you". The early manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: who makes leather
decisions.reason: As at 10:6.

records.source: ἐξαυτῆς οὖν ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, σύ τε καλῶς ἐποίησας παραγενόμενος.
records.gloss: At once therefore I sent to you, you and well did having come.
pieces: I sent for you right away, and it was good of you to come.

L.33: So I sent to you at once, and you have done well to come.

R.33: So I sent for you right away. Thank you for coming.

decisions.choice: you have done well to come: a polite word of thanks
alternatives: a judgment that Peter obeyed God
decisions.reason: The phrase is a common courtesy, meaning "thank you for coming", as in 3 John 6.

decisions.choice: Thank you for coming
alternatives: you have done well to come
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the courtesy.

records.source: νῦν οὖν πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πάρεσμεν ἀκοῦσαι πάντα τὰ προστεταγμένα σοι ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου.
records.gloss: Now therefore all we before the God are present to hear all the things having been commanded you by the Lord.
pieces: Now we are all here before God, ready to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to say."

L.33: So now we are all here in the presence of God to hear all the things that have been commanded you by the Lord."

R.33: Now we are all here, and God is here with us. We want to hear everything the Lord has told you to say to us."

decisions.choice: before God: in God's presence, aware that he is listening
decisions.reason: Cornelius knows that God has sent Peter. The gathering listens as people standing before God.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God
decisions.reason: Cornelius knows God, who sent the angel, but has not yet heard of Jesus as Lord (10:36).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "by the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "by God". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God is here with us
decisions.reason: Readable explains "before God" as being in God's presence.

records.source: Ἀνοίξας δὲ Πέτρος τὸ στόμα εἶπεν· Ἐπ’ ἀληθείας καταλαμβάνομαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολήμπτης ὁ θεός, ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ ἔθνει ὁ φοβούμενος αὐτὸν καὶ ἐργαζόμενος δικαιοσύνην δεκτὸς αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
records.gloss: Having opened then Peter the mouth said, Of truth I perceive that not is a receiver of faces the God, \v 35 but in every nation the [one] fearing him and working righteousness acceptable to him is.
pieces: Then Peter began to speak: "In truth I now see that God does not favor one person over another.
Instead, in every nation {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accepts those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and practice righteousness.

L.34: Then Peter opened [his] mouth and said, "In truth I perceive that God is not one who shows partiality,
L.35: but in every nation the one who fears {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and does righteousness is acceptable to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.34: Then Peter began to speak. He said, "This is the truth: I now understand that God treats all people the same.
R.35: He accepts people from every nation who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and live righteous lives.

decisions.choice: one who shows partiality: literally a receiver of faces, one who favors people for who they are outwardly
alternatives: one who judges unfairly in a court only
decisions.reason: The Greek word is built from a Hebrew idiom, to "lift up the face" of someone, meaning to show them favor (Leviticus 19:15, Deuteronomy 10:17). Paul says the same of God in Romans 2:11. God does not favor Jews over Gentiles because of their birth.

decisions.choice: opened his mouth: began to speak at length and solemnly
decisions.reason: The phrase introduces a weighty speech, as in 8:35 and Matthew 5:2.

decisions.choice: in truth: truly, it is really so
alternatives: a statement about the truth of the gospel
decisions.reason: The phrase means "indeed", as in 4:27. Peter has come to see it through the vision and Cornelius's story.

decisions.choice: acceptable to him: welcome to God, whatever their nation
alternatives: already saved by their good works
decisions.reason: Peter does not say that Cornelius is saved without hearing the message: the angel sent for Peter so that Cornelius would hear words by which he would be saved (11:14), and Peter goes on to speak of forgiveness through believing in Jesus (10:43). He says that a person's nation is no barrier to God.

decisions.choice: does righteousness: does what is right in God's sight
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a way of life, as Cornelius's prayers and gifts show (10:2).

decisions.choice: does not favor one person over another / treats all people the same
alternatives: is not a receiver of faces
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal uses the standard English phrase for it.

decisions.choice: live righteous lives
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key word "righteous" in a natural phrase.

records.heading: God does not favor one person over another

records.source: τὸν λόγον ὃν ἀπέστειλεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ εὐαγγελιζόμενος εἰρήνην διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν πάντων κύριος.
records.gloss: The word which he sent to the sons of Israel proclaiming good news of peace through Jesus Christ, this one is of all Lord,
pieces: This is the message {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent to the people of Israel, bringing the good news that peace has come through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and Jesus is Lord of all.

L.36: The word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent to the sons of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (this one is Lord of all),

R.36: This is the message God sent to the people of Israel. It is the good news of peace that comes through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Jesus is Lord over all people.

decisions.choice: the word that he sent: the opening of a sentence Peter does not finish; it points to what his hearers know (10:37)
alternatives: a separate sentence: "he sent the word"
decisions.reason: The phrase stands without a verb of its own. It is most easily read with "you know" in 10:37, as the first of the things Peter's hearers know. Peter's Greek is broken here, as in a speech that pours out.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the word which he sent"
alternatives: several early manuscripts lack "which": "he sent the word to the sons of Israel"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts do not have the relative pronoun, which makes the verse a simple sentence: God sent the word to Israel. Other early manuscripts and most later ones have it, and the SBLGNT prints it. The sense is close either way. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: he sent his word ... good news of peace: the words of Psalm 107:20 and Isaiah 52:7
decisions.reason: In the Greek of Psalm 107:20 God "sent his word and healed them", and Isaiah 52:7 speaks of the feet of one who brings good news of peace. The one who sent is God.

decisions.choice: peace through Jesus Christ: peace with God, which also makes peace between peoples
decisions.reason: The message brings reconciliation with God; here, in a Gentile house, it also brings Jews and Gentiles together (Ephesians 2:17, which also echoes Isaiah 52:7).

decisions.choice: this one is Lord of all: Jesus is Lord of all people, Gentiles as well as Jews
decisions.reason: The word "all" could be people or things. In this setting, where God shows no partiality between nations, it means Lord of Jews and Gentiles alike, as Romans 10:12 says.

decisions.choice: This is the message
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Peter's unfinished phrase a full sentence; the meaning note explains the Greek.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who sent the message.

decisions.choice: Christ, with "Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere.

records.source: ὑμεῖς οἴδατε τὸ γενόμενον ῥῆμα καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐκήρυξεν Ἰωάννης, Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει, ὃς διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: you know the having happened thing throughout all the Judea, having begun from the Galilee after the baptism which proclaimed John, \v 38 Jesus the from Nazareth, how anointed him the God with Spirit Holy and with power, who went about doing good and healing all those being oppressed by the devil, because the God was with him.
pieces: You yourselves know the events that took place across all Judea. They began in Galilee, after the baptism John proclaimed.

They concern Jesus from Nazareth: God anointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with the Holy Spirit and with power, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} traveled from place to place doing good and healing everyone the devil held in his grip, because God was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.37: you yourselves know the thing that happened throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed:
L.38: Jesus from Nazareth, how God anointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with [the] Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.37: You know about the things that happened in all the land of the Jews. They started in Galilee, after John told people to be baptized.
R.38: You know about Jesus from Nazareth. God poured out the Holy Spirit and power on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and so made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Anointed One. Jesus went everywhere doing good things. He healed all the people whom the devil was hurting and controlling, because God was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power: God set Jesus apart as the Christ, the Anointed One
decisions.reason: The verb "anoint" is the root of the title Christ, the Anointed One. Kings and priests were anointed with oil; Jesus was anointed with the Spirit at his baptism (Luke 3:22). In Nazareth he read Isaiah 61:1, "the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me", and said it was fulfilled (Luke 4:18-21). Compare 4:27.

decisions.choice: all Judea: the whole land of the Jews, including Galilee
decisions.reason: Here Judea means the whole Jewish homeland, since it began in Galilee, as in Luke 23:5.

decisions.choice: beginning from Galilee: the events began there; the word agrees loosely with the sentence
decisions.reason: The participle does not fit the grammar neatly, like the start of 10:36. The sense is clear: the story began in Galilee.

decisions.choice: Jesus from Nazareth, how God anointed him: the subject of what they know is put first
alternatives: Jesus is the one who knows
decisions.reason: Greek often names the person first and then says what is known about him: "you know about Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him".

decisions.choice: oppressed by the devil: held under the devil's power, by sickness and by evil spirits
decisions.reason: The verb means to overpower or dominate. Luke counts both sickness and evil spirits among the devil's works (Luke 13:16).

decisions.choice: God was with him: God's presence and power were at work in Jesus
alternatives: Jesus was only a good man
decisions.reason: Peter speaks first of what his hearers could see; he goes on to call Jesus Lord of all (10:36) and judge of the living and the dead (10:42). Nicodemus says the same of Jesus's signs (John 3:2).

decisions.choice: God poured out the Holy Spirit and power on him, and so made him the Christ, the Anointed One
alternatives: God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power
decisions.reason: Readable explains anointing and links it to the title Christ, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: everyone the devil held in his grip / whom the devil was hurting and controlling
alternatives: all who were oppressed by the devil
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the picture of oppression in plainer words.

decisions.choice: after John told people to be baptized
alternatives: after the baptism that John proclaimed
decisions.reason: Readable explains that John called people to be baptized (Luke 3:3).

records.source: καὶ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρες πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἔν τε τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· ὃν καὶ ἀνεῖλαν κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου.
records.gloss: And we [are] witnesses of all things which he did in both the region of the Jews and Jerusalem; whom also they killed having hanged on a tree.
pieces: We ourselves saw all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, both in the Jewish countryside and in Jerusalem, and we testify to it. Yet they put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, hanging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on a tree.

L.39: And we are witnesses of all things that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem; and they killed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by hanging [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] on a tree.

R.39: We apostles saw everything Jesus did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem, and we tell people about it. But the people of Jerusalem and their leaders killed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They nailed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a wooden cross.

decisions.choice: we are witnesses: the apostles saw these things and tell of them
decisions.reason: A witness in Acts is one who saw and now testifies (1:8, 1:22, 2:32). Those with Peter from Joppa were not among them.

decisions.choice: hanging him on a tree: the words of Deuteronomy 21:22-23
decisions.reason: The law said that anyone hanged on a tree was under God's curse. Peter used the same words before the council (5:30); Paul explains them in Galatians 3:13.

decisions.choice: they killed: the people of Jerusalem and their rulers
decisions.reason: Peter has said the same in 2:23, 3:15 and 5:30. Here the subject is understood from "Jerusalem"; 13:27-28 speaks of those living in Jerusalem and their rulers.

decisions.choice: saw ... and we testify to it / tell people about it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say both sides of being a witness, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: nailed him to a wooden cross
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "hanging on a tree" refers to; Literal and Balanced keep the words of the law.

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem and their leaders
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν ἐμφανῆ γενέσθαι, οὐ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἀλλὰ μάρτυσι τοῖς προκεχειροτονημένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡμῖν, οἵτινες συνεφάγομεν καὶ συνεπίομεν αὐτῷ μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
records.gloss: This one the God raised on the third day and gave him visible to become, \v 41 not to all the people but to witnesses those having been chosen beforehand by the God, to us, who ate with and drank with him after the rising of him from [the] dead;
pieces: God raised this same Jesus on the third day and allowed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to appear openly,

though not to the whole people. He appeared to witnesses whom God had chosen ahead of time, to us. We ate and drank with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had risen from the dead.

L.40: This one God raised on the third day and granted that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} become visible,
L.41: not to all the people, but to witnesses chosen beforehand by God, to us, who ate and drank with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rose from [the] dead;

R.40: But on the third day God raised Jesus back to life. God let people see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
R.41: but not everyone. Only some people saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the ones God had chosen before to be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} witnesses. We are those people. We ate and drank with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to life.

decisions.choice: granted that he become visible: God let the risen Jesus be seen
decisions.reason: The phrase stresses that Jesus was really seen; 10:41 adds that they ate and drank with him (Luke 24:41-43).

decisions.choice: witnesses chosen beforehand by God: God chose who would see the risen Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb means to appoint ahead of time. Jesus chose the apostles (1:2), and God gave them this task (1:8, 1:22).

decisions.choice: ate and drank with him: proof that he had risen bodily
decisions.reason: Luke tells how the risen Jesus ate in front of the disciples (Luke 24:41-43; Acts 1:4).

decisions.choice: all the people: the people of Israel as a whole
decisions.reason: "The people" again means Israel (10:2, 10:42).

decisions.choice: God let people see him
decisions.reason: Readable puts the phrase simply.

decisions.choice: everyone
decisions.reason: Readable shortens the phrase; the meaning note says who the people are.

records.source: καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν.
records.gloss: and he commanded us to proclaim to the people and to testify that this one is the [one] having been appointed by the God judge of living and dead.
pieces: He gave us orders to announce this to the people and to declare solemnly that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one God has appointed as judge of the living and of the dead.

L.42: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded us to proclaim to the people and to testify solemnly that this is the one appointed by God [as] judge of [the] living and [the] dead.

R.42: Jesus told us to preach to the people. He told us to tell them clearly that God has chosen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be the judge of all people, those who are alive and those who have died.

decisions.choice: he commanded: the risen Jesus gave the command
decisions.reason: The subject could be God, the subject of 10:40. But the command to the witnesses comes from Jesus after he rose (1:2, 1:8; Luke 24:47-48).

decisions.choice: the people: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 10:41; the message then reaches the Gentiles too, as here in Cornelius's house.

decisions.choice: appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead: Jesus will judge all people, at his coming
decisions.reason: Paul says the same in Athens (17:31). "The living and the dead" means everyone who has ever lived (2 Timothy 4:1, 1 Peter 4:5).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, as the meaning note explains, and marks the choice as uncertain.

decisions.choice: the judge of all people, those who are alive and those who have died
alternatives: judge of the living and the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pair means.

records.source: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν.
records.gloss: To this one all the prophets bear witness, forgiveness of sins to receive through the name of him everyone the [one] believing in him.
pieces: Every one of the prophets bears witness to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: whoever believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} has their sins forgiven through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."

L.43: To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} receives forgiveness of sins through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."

R.43: All the prophets wrote about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said that God forgives the sins of everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because of who Jesus is and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done."

decisions.choice: all the prophets bear witness: the Scriptures as a whole point to Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter does not quote one text. Jesus taught that the law, the prophets and the psalms speak of him (Luke 24:27, 24:44-47), and Peter said all the prophets announced these days (3:18, 3:24). Isaiah 53:5-6, 53:11 and Jeremiah 31:34 speak of sins taken away.

decisions.choice: through his name: through who he is and what he has done
alternatives: by saying his name as a formula
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person, as in 3:16 and 4:12.

decisions.choice: everyone who believes in him: anyone at all, Jew or Gentile
decisions.reason: "Everyone" is the point of this speech: God has no favorites (10:34). As Peter says it, the Spirit falls on his Gentile hearers (10:44).

decisions.choice: because of who Jesus is and what he has done
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: God forgives the sins
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives.

records.source: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον.
records.gloss: Still speaking the Peter the words these fell the Spirit the Holy upon all those hearing the word.
pieces: Peter was still saying these things when the Holy Spirit came down on everyone who was listening to the message.

L.44: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were hearing the word.

R.44: Peter was still speaking when the Holy Spirit came on all the people who were listening to the message.

decisions.choice: fell upon: came suddenly and powerfully
decisions.reason: Peter says in 11:15 that the Spirit fell on them as on the apostles at the beginning (2:1-4). It happened before Peter had finished, and before anyone was baptized or had hands laid on them (compare 8:17).

decisions.choice: the word: the message about Jesus that Peter was speaking
decisions.reason: As in 10:36 and 4:4, "the word" is the message of the gospel.

decisions.choice: came down on / came on
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a plainer verb; Literal keeps "fell", the word Peter repeats in 11:15.

records.heading: The gift of the Spirit poured out on Gentiles

records.source: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐκκέχυται·
records.gloss: And were amazed the from circumcision believers as many as came with the Peter, that also upon the Gentiles the gift of the Holy Spirit has been poured out;
pieces: The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on Gentiles too.

L.45: And the believers from [the] circumcision who had come with Peter were amazed, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles;

R.45: The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed. God had given the Holy Spirit as a gift even to people who were not Jews!

decisions.choice: the believers from the circumcision: Jewish believers
alternatives: a party that insisted on circumcision
decisions.reason: Here the phrase simply means the believers who were Jews by birth, the brothers from Joppa (10:23). In 11:2 a similar phrase names those in Jerusalem who objected.

decisions.choice: poured out: the words of Joel's prophecy
decisions.reason: Peter quoted Joel at Pentecost: God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh (2:17-18, 2:33; Joel 3:1-2 in the Hebrew numbering). Now that includes Gentiles.

decisions.choice: the gift of the Holy Spirit: the gift that is the Spirit himself
decisions.reason: As in 2:38; 11:17 says God gave them the same gift.

decisions.choice: people who were not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles".

decisions.choice: God had given the Holy Spirit as a gift
alternatives: the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver, as the passive implies, and puts the gift as the Spirit himself.

records.source: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν θεόν.
records.gloss: they were hearing for them speaking in tongues and magnifying the God.
pieces: For they heard them speaking in tongues and praising the greatness of God.

L.46: for they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God.

R.46: They knew this because they heard these people speaking in tongues, as the believers did at Pentecost, and praising God for how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

decisions.choice: speaking in tongues: speech given by the Spirit, as at Pentecost
decisions.reason: At Pentecost the believers spoke in languages that hearers from many nations understood (2:4-11). Peter says these Gentiles received the same gift as the apostles at the beginning (11:15, 11:17), but Luke does not say whether anyone here understood the languages.

decisions.choice: magnifying God: praising God's greatness
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare great, as in Luke 1:46. At Pentecost too the believers spoke of the mighty works of God (2:11).

decisions.choice: as the believers did at Pentecost
decisions.reason: Readable draws the link that Peter himself draws in 11:15.

records.source: τότε ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος·
records.gloss: Then answered Peter,
pieces: Then Peter said,

decisions.choice: answered: responded to what had happened
decisions.reason: No one had asked anything. The verb often means to respond to a situation, here to the Spirit's coming.

decisions.choice: said
decisions.reason: Since no one asked a question, Balanced and Readable say "said".

records.source: Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ δύναται κωλῦσαί τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους οἵτινες τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔλαβον ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς;
records.gloss: Not the water is able to forbid anyone, the not to be baptized these, who the Spirit the Holy received as also we?
pieces: "Surely no one can refuse the water to keep these people from being baptized. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we did!"

L.47: "Can anyone withhold the water, so that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we also [did]?"

R.47: "These people have received the Holy Spirit, just as we did. So no one can stop them from being baptized with water!"

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no: no one can refuse them baptism
decisions.reason: The Greek form of the question expects "no". Peter recalls this in 11:17: who was he to stand in God's way?

decisions.choice: who have received the Holy Spirit just as we did: God has already accepted them
decisions.reason: Peter reasons from what God has done. In 15:8-9 he says God gave them the Spirit and made no distinction between them and the Jews.

decisions.choice: withhold: forbid, prevent
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 8:36 and 11:17, and of children in Luke 18:16.

decisions.choice: a statement rather than a question
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the answer the question expects.

records.source: προσέταξεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι.
records.gloss: He commanded and them in the name of Jesus Christ to be baptized.
pieces: So he gave orders for them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.48: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.48: So Peter told them to be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus Christ: calling on Jesus and coming under his authority
decisions.reason: As in 2:38 and 8:16.

decisions.choice: he commanded them to be baptized: Peter gave the order; others may have baptized them
decisions.reason: The Greek says Peter ordered it, not who did it, as Paul often left baptizing to others (1 Corinthians 1:14-17).

decisions.choice: Christ, with "Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere.

records.source: τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς.
records.gloss: Then they asked him to remain days some.
pieces: Then they asked him to stay on with them for a few days.

L.48: Then they asked him to stay some days.

R.48: Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few more days.

decisions.choice: to stay some days: as their guest, eating and lodging in a Gentile house
decisions.reason: Staying with Gentiles is what the believers in Jerusalem criticized: "you went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them" (11:3).
